Lesson5.3-other-agentic-software-factories 5.3-other-agentic-software-factories

Inside Uber's Software Factory

Uber gives the fullest account of realization increasing at organizational scale: more than 70 percent of pull requests attributed to local or cloud agents, more than 3,600 engineer-created agent skills executing over 30,000 times per day, managed agents performing code review, CI repair, end-to-end changes, alert triage, debugging, and maintenance.[cite: medisetty2026factory] What new work inherits is the interesting structure: real workloads become benchmarks; models are selected against cost, quality, and reliability; context and tool access are compiled down to reduce unnecessary reasoning; recurring workflows harden into reusable skills — in one example, deterministic tool orchestration moves out of repeated model turns into executable code, cutting token use by more than half on common workflows and by more than 90 percent in bulk cases.[cite: medisetty2026factory] Supervision is structured by measurement: managed agents are evaluated in units such as cost per merged pull request, review, or alert.

Inside GitLab's Software Factory

GitLab starts from the other end: as code becomes abundant, the scarce problem shifts to trusting it.

Inside Cloudflare's Software Factory

Cloudflare gives the cleanest policy-first entry.

Inside Siemens's Software Factory

Siemens enters from outside software-first engineering, and that is exactly its value.

Inside Docker's Software Factory

Docker's system separates delegated roles, tool permissions, implementation, and evaluation: seven permission-backed roles, an independent reviewer running on a separate model invocation, and deterministic tests supplying repeatable evidence.[cite: delapena2026fleet] Realization and evaluation are both substantially mechanized; final admission deliberately is not.

Inside Spotify's Software Factory

Spotify's Honk system moves large-scale code migration from distributed manual implementation toward centrally scoped, fleet-executed work: a migration that could previously involve hundreds of teams over weeks can be scoped by one engineer over a few days, with tooling identifying and scheduling targets, agents executing changes concurrently, and the engineer supervising the fleet and handling exceptions.[cite: spotify2026honk] The inheritance is the estate representation — a system model and service catalog carrying identities, ownership, dependencies, and lineage — through which migrations are targeted rather than rediscovered per repository.

Inside Shopify's Software Factory

Shopify's account describes agent work occurring in shared, observable channels rather than private sessions — one month's snapshot counts 59,918 sessions across 5,170 channels involving more than 7,000 people, "multiplayer by construction."[cite: moreno2026river] Shared sessions become searchable organizational artifacts; recurring knowledge is extracted into skills, conventions, and defaults later agents retrieve.

Inside Zenseact's Software Factory

Zenseact, building driver-assistance software, describes an organizational split: a platform team owns common substrate — authentication, sessions, execution, and the safety envelope — while domain teams retain their own agents, tools, instructions, and expertise.[cite: dufwa2026zap] Routing machinery selects task-relevant expertise instead of loading the whole organizational corpus into every reasoning window.

What the Factories Share, and Where They Differ

Across the eight accounts, four moves recur strongly enough to form a shared baseline.

The Engineers Inside the Factories

The eight accounts above are institutional self-descriptions — engineering blogs and vendor architecture papers, systems presented at their best.

Lesson7.4-the-engineer 7.4-the-engineer

Authority Follows Competence and Responsibility

MAGE increases both the leverage of engineering knowledge and the consequences of getting it wrong.

Professional authority

Engineering authority extends beyond technical capability.

The judgment frontier

One social purpose of the engineer is to be entrusted with, and answerable for, technical work too complex or consequential for ordinary individuals to undertake for themselves.[cite: bugliarello-social-function] A small bridge across the ditch in my parents' yard allowed the neighborhood kids to visit more easily, but a few boards crossing a span of three feet did not call for a structural engineer.

Sign-Off Moves Toward Models and Evidence

Imagine an agentic system in which the fleet constructs most of the implementation, maintains selected engineering representations, runs validators, and assembles evidence for the claims the design is supposed to satisfy.

From Full-Stack to Full-System Engineering

Software has used full-stack engineer to describe someone able to work across multiple implementation layers: interface, application logic, data, infrastructure, and deployment.

What Should We Teach?

If engineers increasingly review systems through representations and evidence rather than reconstructing every property from implementation, education should shift accordingly.

Is there software engineering knowledge you cannot just figure out for yourself?

The question for software engineering education is whether there is important software engineering knowledge that practitioners cannot reasonably be expected to figure out for themselves, or whether software engineering is distinct among the engineering disciplines in being predicated on adaptability more than specific expertise.

What shouldn't software engineers have to figure out for themselves?

I would concede some of this ground.

Shift the emphasis

Less educational effort may need to go toward producing routine implementation by hand, and more toward selecting abstractions, specifying properties, measuring systems, validating claims, reasoning about quality attributes, and governing autonomous work.

A capstone should therefore demonstrate more than a working artifact.
